title: WAMs and VLAs for Robot Learning | Cosmos Labs
summary: NVIDIA’s Cosmos Labs livestream lays out how World Action Models and vision-language-action models play different roles in robot foundation models, with WAMs modeling future observations and actions while VLAs connect perception, language, and control. It centers on Cosmos 3, which treats action as a native modality alongside video, and shows how Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID can imagine future observations while generating robot actions. The session is framed as a practical path for adapting and deploying these models with open Cosmos models, datasets, recipes, evaluation workflows, and serving resources.

extra.full_text: Building capable robot foundation models requires more than one approach. Vision-language-action (VLA) models and World Action Models (WAMs) - each offer different strengths for robot learning, planning, and control. In this livestream, NVIDIA researchers Danfei Xu US Moritz Benno Reuss CH Thomas Tian US will explore what World Action Models work, how they compare with modern Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and why many next-generation robot foundation models combine both approaches. You'll also see how NVIDIA Cosmos 3 treats action as a native modality, enabling robots to predict future observations while generating actions. We'll walk through how Cosmos 3 provides an open workflow for post-training, evaluation, and deployment using open models, datasets, recipes, and serving resources. Whether you're building manipulation policies, training robot foundation models, or exploring embodied AI, this livestream provides a practical understanding of where World Action Models fit into the future of robotics. What You'll Learn: - What World Action Models are and how they differ from and complement Vision-Language-Action models - The strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs of WAMs, VLAs, and emerging hybrid approaches - How Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID imagines future observations while generating robot actions - How NVIDIA Cosmos 3 represents action as a native modality alongside video - How to evaluate, post-train, and adapt Cosmos 3 using open models, datasets, recipes, and serving resources Have questions about how to post-train and deploy NVIDIA Cosmos 3? Drop them live — the NVIDIA team will answer them in real time. title: Robots Doing Stuff #63 | Failure Recovery Montage
summary: Sanctuary AI showed a failure-recovery montage for its Physical AI policy on an industrial plug-insertion task, emphasizing how the robot adapts when parts shift or the setup deviates from the expected cycle. The same task was previously reported at over 99.5% success with a 2.54-second cycle time, and the new demo highlights recovery from unexpected states as the practical lever for reducing human intervention and keeping throughput stable in less repeatable production environments.

extra.full_text: Why are some industrial tasks impossible to automate with traditional methods? Because real-world environments aren't perfectly repeatable. Parts shift and conditions change from cycle to cycle. Our production-ready Physical AI enables robotic systems to adapt to these changing conditions, helping recover from unexpected situations, reduce manual intervention, and maintain throughput. In short: our policies are as tenacious as we are. Back in June, we shared this plug insertion task achieving 99.5%+ success at a cycle time of 2.54 seconds. This week, we're showing another aspect of the same policy with a failure recovery montage. #SanctuaryAI #Robotics #PhysicalAI #Automation #IndustrialRobots #RobotsDoingStuff #SanctuaryAI Visit www.sanctuary.ai to learn more about our Physical AI-enabled automation solutions.

title: AI 수술로봇 개발 현장 찾은 조달청장…첨단기술 현장 행보
summary: Korea’s Public Procurement Service visited Roen Surgical at KAIST’s Munji Campus to review development of an AI-based surgical robot and discuss how innovative procurement can help advanced medical products reach public-sector users. Roen’s kidney-stone surgery robot, Zamenix, uses AI and laser technology to precisely fragment and remove renal stones, and after being designated an innovative procurement product last year, it is now being validated through a pilot purchase at the National Medical Center.
